summary: This video is a hands-on, field-to-finish workflow for creating large panoramas from drone imagery, with emphasis on correcting stitching artifacts, choosing appropriate projections, and performing advanced post-processing. The presenter compares DJI’s native stitching to PTGui’s capabilities, demonstrates automatic exposure matching across images, and walks through assembling, saving, and post-processing a panorama in Photoshop. The session includes handling both wide-field desert canyon scenes and night/morning shots, discusses sky management (including the necessity of sky content for reliable pano stitching), focal stacking workflows (including manual sun-star fixes), and creative color grading techniques (including 50-150 color separation). The talk also covers practical tips about RAW vs JPEG pipelines, working with very large image sets, and the realities of processing in the field across diverse locations such as the American Southwest (Hanksville, Mono Lake, Zion, Kofa) and mentions of New Zealand, Norway, and Pakistan as trip contexts.

sections.title: Field stitching realities and distortion
concepts: Edge cropping and extra image space
Rectilinear distortion benefits and horizon cues
sections.description: Introduction to DJI stitching limitations (edges cropped, extra content around stitched frames) and the rectilinear distortion that helps lines converge. Mention that Lightroom stitching can yield a curved horizon, illustrating why a rectilinear projection may be preferred in certain panos.

sections.title: Panorama search and projection options
concepts: Projection options in PTGui vs Lightroom
sections.description: The presenter locates 0472 panorama files, explains that PTGui provides more projection options (rectilinear, cylindrical, stereographic, etc.) and demonstrates choosing rectilinear to preserve leading lines toward the sun.

sections.title: Initial PTGui alignment and exposure handling
sections.description: In PTGui, the workflow begins with selecting the panorama set (0472 panorama) and aligning images. Demonstrates how PTGui pre-aligns and matches exposures across frames before stitching, contrasting with Lightroom’s more limited automatic exposure handling.

sections.title: Panorama creation and file export
sections.description: Demonstrates choosing the panorama output (TIFF) and where to save (card), as well as the speed of stitching once parameters are set.

sections.title: From PTGui to Photoshop prep
sections.description: Back in Photoshop, the stitched panorama is opened, cropped to improve composition (rule of thirds), and image dimensions adjusted for more natural aspect ratio.

sections.title: Two-zone post-processing workflow
sections.description: Describes breaking the image into foreground and sky zones in Camera Raw, performing opposite adjustments to foreground and sky, and addressing flare and sun-star behavior with layered edits.

sections.title: Enhancing depth with diffusion and color grading
sections.description: Explains diffusion around the sun area to create glow, followed by color grading and multiple gradient steps to harmonize foreground and sky while maintaining horizon integrity.

sections.title: Framing, timing, and desert landscapes in the Southwest
sections.description: Elaborates on timing opportunities (late August, early May) for the Southwest desert; discusses how light beams through canyons, desert wildflowers, and the impact of light direction on the final image.

sections.title: Large panoramas, sky content, and control points
sections.description: Addresses challenges of stitching huge panoramas, the necessity of having sky/clouds for successful stitching, and notes on control-point work and potential limitations when sky data are insufficient.

sections.title: Focus stacking and multi-shot composites
sections.description: Discusses extensive focus stacking workflows, working with many RAW captures, and the interaction between stacking and sky; includes details on Photoshop scripts, auto-align, auto-blend, and using content-aware fill to fix gaps.

sections.title: Color management, advanced color grading, and refinement
sections.description: Covers advanced color separation (50-150), selective color corrections, multiple color-grade passes, and the use of vignetting to guide viewer attention. Also addresses issues with magenta-green shifts and how to harmonize complex layers.

sections.title: Moon shots, black & white processing, and final polish
sections.description: Concludes with moon-shot processing in black and white using dodge/burn, discusses the controversial Orton effect, and emphasizes the speed and flexibility of processing with a tripod versus handheld. Ends with reflections on final exports and the importance of preserving natural look.
